job_description:
Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Scientist I to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

The Data Scientist I supports research, analytics, and data-driven decision-making. This role partners with research teams to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret data to deliver meaningful insights for clients and stakeholders.

The position is responsible for importing, cleaning, standardizing, transforming, and validating data, identifying data quality issues, and developing reports and visualizations. The Data Scientist I may also support data management processes, and proposal development activities. This role works collaboratively in a team-oriented environment.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Sciences Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

• Collect, clean, transform, validate, and harmonize data from a variety of sources.
• Identify trends, patterns, and data quality issues, and communicate findings and recommendations to project teams and stakeholders.
• Develop reports, dashboards, tables, charts, and visualizations.
• Create, document, manage, and maintain databases, data systems, and data dictionaries.
• Support data storage optimization and data management procedures.
• Collaborate with research teams, project leaders, and clients to understand analytical needs and support project objectives.
• Contribute to proposal development activities, including drafting technical or analytical sections.

Required Skills

• Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required. Advanced degree preferred.
• Proficiency with data management and data processing.
• 4 years of experience in positions of increasing responsibility, working with large data sets and conducting statistical/analytic programming, preferably working with large data sets
• Strong foundation in areas of statistics, mathematics, and data science.
• Advanced programming skills in SAS are required, including experience with SAS macros
• Additional experience with other statistical packages and database tools such as SQL, Python, R, Tableau, Hadoop, Hive, MapReduce and/or other large data systems is welcome but not essential.
• Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is strongly preferred.
• Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required. Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
• Outstanding interpersonal and critical reasoning skills.
• Strong written and verbal communication including strong technical writing skills.
• Strong data visualization/presentation skills. Able to explain technology, techniques, and approaches to others.
• Proficiency with MS Office software.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $90,000-$104,000

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
• Dental and vision insurance
• A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
• Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
• Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Data Scientist / Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support a classified government contract. The successful candidate will provide technical expertise in analyzing and interpreting complex data to inform enterprise data management decisions, identify opportunities for the application of Data Science, and develop innovative solutions that address customer mission requirements.

The Data Scientist will support multiple customer organizations and Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO) initiatives by identifying and evaluating opportunities to apply advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to customer data assets. The position will help bridge the gap between mission requirements, data assets, and emerging AI/ML capabilities.

The role requires extensive collaboration with government stakeholders, technical teams, external customers, and IC partners. The Data Scientist will contribute to the development and implementation of technical solutions, support integration of AI capabilities with existing customer data environments, and help establish repeatable approaches for leveraging Data Science across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as a Data Science SME providing technical leadership and expertise across customer organizations and mission areas.
• Analyze, interpret, and derive insights from complex, heterogeneous, and large-scale datasets to support mission and enterprise decision-making.
• Identify opportunities to apply Data Science, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to customer mission challenges.
• Assess customer data assets to determine their suitability for advanced analytics and AI/ML applications.
• Support CAIO initiatives by identifying, evaluating, prioritizing, and implementing Data Science and AI use cases.
• Translate mission and business requirements into Data Science problems, analytical approaches, technical requirements, and implementation strategies.
• Develop statistical models, machine learning models, algorithms, and analytical methodologies to address complex customer requirements.
• Design and develop prototypes and proof-of-concept solutions to demonstrate the potential value of Data Science and AI capabilities.
• Support the transition of successful prototypes and analytical capabilities into operational or production environments.
• Integrate AI and Data Science solutions with existing customer data assets, platforms, pipelines, and analytic environments.
• Collaborate with data engineers, data architects, software developers, AI/ML engineers, and other technical personnel to develop end-to-end solutions.
• Provide technical support to other customer organizations seeking to identify and implement Data Science opportunities.
• Coordinate with external customers, mission partners, IC organizations, and other stakeholders to define requirements and develop interoperable technical solutions.
• Participate in technical working groups, design sessions, and collaborative forums focused on Data Science, AI, and enterprise data capabilities.
• Evaluate emerging Data Science, AI/ML, and analytical technologies and recommend capabilities that can improve customer mission effectiveness.
• Assess data quality, availability, structure, provenance, and other characteristics that may affect analytical and AI solution development.
• Identify data management challenges and recommend improvements required to enable effective Data Science and AI applications.
• Develop reusable analytical methodologies, models, frameworks, and technical approaches that can be applied across multiple customer organizations.
• Support development of standards, best practices, and repeatable processes for Data Science experimentation, evaluation, implementation, and operationalization.
• Develop analytical documentation, technical specifications, model documentation, methodologies, and implementation plans.
• Validate analytical models and results and communicate assumptions, limitations, risks, and findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Brief government leadership and mission stakeholders on Data Science opportunities, analytical findings, technical approaches, and recommendations.
• Serve as a trusted technical advisor on the application of Data Science and AI to customer data and mission requirements.
• Ensure all solutions and activities comply with applicable security, classification, data governance, privacy, and customer policies.

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our senior Research Scientists, Statisticians, and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location : This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Science Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

• Collaborate with researchers, statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management, processing, and analysis activities.
• Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
• Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
• Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
• Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

• Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required.
• Proficiency with data management and data processing.
• 0-2 years’ experience in positions of increasing responsibility, preferably working with large data sets, and conducting statistical/analytic programming (internships included).
• Strong foundation in areas of statistics, mathematics, and data science.
• Proficient coding skills in SAS are required, including experience with SAS macros
• Additional experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential.
• Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred.
• Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required. Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
• Outstanding interpersonal and critical reasoning skills.
• Proficiency with MS Office software.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000 – $77,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
• Dental and vision insurance
• A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
• Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
• Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.
